instruction_covers: Analysis must reject a dispense when the pipette never aspirated
Analysis must reject a dispense whose volume exceeds what was previously aspirated
Both cases fail with a dedicated error type named InvalidDispenseVolumeError
The check applies to protocols on apiLevel 2.15+
label: suspect
notes: Repo verified: VirtualPipettingHandler.dispense_in_place (api/src/opentrons/protocol_engine/execution/pipetting.py) validates only push_out and tip, never aspirated volume; get_aspirated_volume returns Optional[float] (None when nothing aspirated); no InvalidDispenseVolumeError exists at base. Grep for 'def dispense' surfaces the dispense_in_place family, and the aspirated-volume guard is directly analogous to the existing aspirate-side validation with no new semantics from R2's list, so the minimal fix of exactly what the instruction asks lands in dispense_in_place and passes. The error module/base/constructor follow the exact sibling pattern of InvalidPushOutVolumeError and InvalidPipettingVolumeError in protocol_engine/errors/exceptions.py (mechanical propagation, not a separate item). Per R2 the unnamed engine method is an item, and per the sound-vs-suspect tie-break (sound means no doubt) the label is at least suspect.

unstated.what: The dispense-without-aspirate / insufficient-aspirated-volume validation (InvalidDispenseVolumeError) must live in VirtualPipettingHandler.dispense_in_place; the instruction describes only user-level pipette.dispense plus analysis and never names the engine method
